title: Surge credit ledger and priority decay for Dedicated tenants
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Problem: Dedicated tenants sometimes need short-lived bursts beyond their reserved throughput for traffic spikes. Current reserved pools + burst policies rely on instantaneous capacity heuristics which lead to: noisy neighbors, non-deterministic fairness, and operator intervention for disputed bursts. This PRD proposes a 'surge credit ledger' combined with a tenant priority decay model to make burst behavior predictable, auditable, and configurable for both customers and platform operators.
problem_statement: Reserved capacity should guarantee baseline throughput while allowing controlled, auditable bursts that can be balanced across tenants without violating SLOs for higher-priority contracts. Today bursts are opaque and can starve other tenants or exhaust safety buffers unexpectedly.
goals: Enable tenants to earn, purchase, or be assigned surge credits that allow short-term burst above baseline reserved throughput
Define a priority decay algorithm so sustained high-usage from a tenant reduces its effective burst priority over a configurable window
Make credits and priority adjustments visible in Console and via API with audit logs and per-tenant ledgers
Provide operator guards and automated fallback policies that preserve cluster-level latency SLOs while honoring tenant-level SLAs
non_goals: Replace existing reservation or burst payment models (this augments them)
Implement per-request pricing changes in billing (billing will consume a separate integration workstream)
Support cross-account credit sharing in this phase
success_metrics: Reduce manual capacity disputes filed by customers by >= 60% in first 90 days post-launch
Maintain 95th percentile p99 token latency for reserved tenants within current SLA under test traffic with aggregate bursts up to 2x baseline
Average fairshare score (internal metric) across tenants improves by 30% during burst storm tests
Console and API ledger read latency < 500ms for tenant queries
user_stories: As a tenant admin, I want to view my surge credit balance and recent ledger entries in the Console so I can understand burst usage history
As a platform operator, I want to see cluster-level surge credit burn rate and flagged tenants with rapid priority decay so I can investigate anomalies
As a system, when a tenant exceeds baseline throughput and has credits, I want to automatically debit credits and allow controlled burst until credits or ceilings are reached
As an SRE, I want automatic fallbacks that gracefully throttle low-priority tenants before impacting reserved SLA holders during capacity degradation
requirements: Surge credit ledger model stored with O(1) read/write per request: balance, last_updated, windowed_burn (implementation detail surfaced as internal metric)
Console: tenant ledger UI showing remaining credits, last 30 days of transactions, and actionable purchase/allocate button
Priority decay algorithm configurable per-tenant-class: parameters (decay_half_life_hours, min_priority, window_seconds)
Cluster-level controller that enforces global safety caps: max_aggregate_burst_percent and emergency_drain_threshold
Audit logs for every credit debit/credit operation with actor, reason, and request_id
Integration with existing routing layer so that when credits exhausted or priority low, requests are routed to fallback model variants or queued according to policy
constraints: Initial implementation must work with existing Dedicated autoscaler and reservation subsystems; avoid invasive runtime changes
Storage for ledger should use existing metadata store (limited QPS) — avoid heavy per-token writes
UI must reuse Console components where possible to meet Q2 timeline
Billing integration is out of scope for MVP and will consume 'adjust' metadata only (currency handled later)
acceptance_criteria: MVP system exposes GET/POST APIs for ledger with appropriate auth and returns consistent balances under concurrent bursts (concurrency tests passing)
Console shows ledger entries and balance for a test tenant and allows operator adjustments (mocked UI data acceptable in first experiment)

Simulated cluster test: with 200 tenants and randomized bursts, system preserves reserved SLA tenants' 95th percentile request latency within current SLA while allowing tenants with credits to exceed baseline up to configured caps
Priority decay works: a tenant that sustains 3x baseline for duration > decay_window sees effective priority drop by configured factor and observed routing changes accordingly in test harness
Audit logs for ledger transactions are emitted and searchable in ELK for at least 30 days (or a test index), and include request_id mapping to production traces
Operator emergency_drain can be triggered via Console and will reduce all non-HIGH priority tenant burst windows within 30s
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Internal experiment (2 sprints): implement ledger backend, in-memory simulator, API endpoints behind feature flag; test with synthetic tenants
Phase 1 - Beta customers (4 sprints): Console UI, config controls, integrate with routing for safe bursts; onboard 3 committed customers for feedback
Phase 2 - GA (2 sprints): polished UI, operator dashboards, runbook, and documentation; toggle on for platform-wide use with opt-in contracts
Post-GA - Billing and Marketplace integration (follow-on): wire credit consumption into billing and allow purchases
risks_mitigations: Risk: Ledger write amplification under high QPS. Mitigation: batch debits in runtime with optimistic concurrency and reconcile asynchronously to canonical store
Risk: Unintended starvation of low-tier tenants during coordinated bursts. Mitigation: implement conservative initial global caps and run fairness simulations before relaxation
Risk: Complexity in priority decay tuning causing customer confusion. Mitigation: ship sane defaults, expose simulator in Console, and include 'explain' traces for adjustments
Risk: Audit log volume causing storage pressure. Mitigation: compress ledger entries older than 7 days and store aggregates for 30/90 day views
dependencies: ENG-42634 (routing-layer: support for dynamic priority weights)
ENG-43710 (console: tenant settings and feature-flag UI framework)
ENG-44021 (auth: RBAC checks for ledger adjustment API)
open_questions: Should acquired credits expire on a fixed cadence (monthly) or use sliding window carryover? Initial proposal: small carryover cap to avoid hoarding
What is the billing model for purchased credits (pre-pay vs post-pay)? Out of scope but needs alignment with finance before GA
How granular should the console simulator be (per-minute vs per-second)? Start with per-minute to reduce data volume
Do we allow operator-issued emergency credits for incidents, and if so, do they bypass decay? Proposal: emergency credits have manual TTL and bypass one decay cycle
